questions.question: Did the Blue Lives Matter Flag show at a Donald trump Rally in Waukesha campaign rally in 2020?

statements.statement: A Thin Blue Line flag, which is a black-and-white version of the American flag with a single blue stripe instead of a red one and is associated with the 'Blue Lives Matter' movement launched in response to the Black Lives Matter movement, was used as a prominent backdrop behind President Donald Trump at his Oct. 24 rally in Waukesha, Wisconsin.
statements.support_span: In a review of photos of the Oct. 24 Waukesha rally taken by the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel, the Thin Blue Line flag is hung prominently behind the risers behind the podium where Trump spoke. | The flag essentially is a black-and-white version of the American flag, with a single red stripe replaced by a blue one. | The company began marketing the flag in 2014, amid the Blue Lives Matter movement, which itself was launched in response to the Black Lives Matter movement.

statements.statement: The Thin Blue Line flag has been used by white supremacist groups alongside Confederate flags in the past, is considered controversial and some community members view it as an overt display of racism, but the Thin Blue Line USA company states the flag is intended to promote compassion and support for police officers rather than being political or hateful.
statements.support_span: At protests in Charlottesville in 2017, where white supremacist groups and supporters gathered to protest the removal of Confederate statues throughout the country, the blue-line flag was featured alongside Confederate flags | A July 31 NPR report highlighted a fight between a Massachusetts fire department flying the flags in honor of fallen police officers and community members who felt the flag was an overt display of racism. | According to the company’s website, the flag is meant to be a sign for “promoting compassion and support for our nation’s police officers.” ... Andrew Jacob, president of Thin Blue Line USA said: “The flag has no association with racism, hatred, bigotry. It’s a flag to show support for law enforcement — no politics involved.”

silver.justification: Evidence confirms that a 'Thin Blue Line' flag, rather than an 'anti-Black Lives Matter' flag, was used as a backdrop behind President Trump at the Waukesha rally. While the Thin Blue Line flag is a black-and-white version of the American flag associated with the 'Blue Lives Matter' movement—which emerged in response to Black Lives Matter—the evidence presents conflicting interpretations of its intent. The manufacturer states the flag is intended to show compassion and support for law enforcement without political or hateful associations; however, the evidence also notes the flag is controversial, has been used by white supremacist groups, and is viewed by some community members as an overt display of racism.
